newsitem.title: USA: CME Depository Trust to become limited partnership.
newsitem.headline: CME Depository Trust to become limited partnership.

text.p: The CME Depository Trust Company said it plans to become a limited partnership by July to prevent an $8 million revenue shortfall for the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, the trust's sole shareholder.

John McPartland, DTC's chief executive, said in an interview the shortfall was projected after the trust's 11 charter members, who signed letters of intent to join DTC last fall, changed the original long-term pricing terms.
DTC recently offered 80 limited partnerships for $100,000 each. It hopes to start the system soon after becoming a limited partnership at the end of July.

The DTC, which has been in development for more than two years and had originally aimed to start in the first quarter of 1997, is an Illinois trust company that will manage collateral for financial institutions and dealers.
The trust will also offer price matching systems through Sungard Capital Markets and the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunications (SWIFT).

McPartland said some of the 11 charter members, who consist of U.S., Asian and European banks and dealers, did not want a fee schedule in which costs would be above market value for the first several years of operation.
"The exchange agreed to commit several millions of dollars to the project before there was a shift in pricing philosophy," he said.
The CME's break-even point would be 16,000 contracts a day if it were to commit $8 million to the trust over two years.
McPartland said the CME has already spent the most ever for an initiative unrelated to its core futures and options floor business, but would not elaborate on the amount spent.
"We need to find another entity that is prepared to absorb the next $8 million in operating losses in return for potential profit," he said.
He expects a limited partner to receive "several multiples of their initial investment" within five years.
Last week the exchange's directors agreed to expand the Depository Trust's board of directors to 11, from 10, with the limited partners selecting five of the 11 directors, he said.
